chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), when a man is seized with a boy in one quilt, both naked, the man would be struck (whipped), and the boy be disciplined. And if he has penetrated and was married, he would be stoned.'

key_terms.ثَقَبَ: Penetrated (specifically in the context of sodomy)
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali (peace be upon him), a primary source of jurisprudence
key_terms.مُحْصَناً: Married or free male who has consummated marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for sodomy according to the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith, sourced from the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), delineates the hadd penalty for sodomy by distinguishing between the adult male and the boy, prescribing flogging and discipline respectively. It further specifies that if the man is muhsan (married and free), he is subject to stoning (rajm) upon proof of penetration, a ruling consistent with Shia jurisprudence. This distinction highlights the nuanced application of hadd punishments based on marital status and the nature of the act.
